ex.5: A 90° change of longitude westwards at 70°S. In the southern hemisphere the straight line (great circle) leaves A heading towards the pole: 270° − 45° = 225°.
ex.12: TOM limits: MTOM 64 400; MLM + trip 61 100; MZFM + take-off fuel 60 400 → 60 400. Traffic = 60 400 − 7400 − 35 500 = 17 500 kg, i.e. 3000 kg more than the 14 500 kg planned.
ex.13: Landing mass at the alternate = DOM + load + final reserve + unused contingency = 33 510 + 7600 + 983 + 102 = 42 195 kg.
ex.17: 189 NAM in 30 min → TAS 378 kt. A 30 kt headwind for 30 min removes 15 NM: 174 NM.
ex.19: Book key prints (b). A transverse Mercator is correct along its central meridian, so it suits areas with a large north–south extent; the correct answer is (a).
ex.38: Same meridian, Q further south: track 180°. Δlat = 71° 23' − 48° 33' = 22° 50' = 1370 NM.
ex.43: Δlong = 160° = 10 h 40 min, east is ahead: 1330 + 1040 = 0010 on 7th January.
ex.51: Radial = 320°T − 10°E = 310° M. To show TO, select the reciprocal: 130°.
ex.56: 750 NM needs HF; at night the lower HF frequency is used: 5649 kHz.
ex.58: Planned reserve = 3.25 + 17 = 20.25 USG. Consumption is running at 80 USG for the trip, so 53 USG remain and 40 USG more are needed, leaving 13 USG — the destination can be reached but not with reserves intact.
ex.70: Book key prints (a). In the southern hemisphere deceleration on an east or west heading makes the compass show an apparent turn towards north (the reverse of 'ANDS' in the northern hemisphere), so the correct answer is (c).
ex.76: GS out 190, home 120. PNR = 4 × 190 × 120 / 310 ≈ 294 NM, leaving 106 NM to Q.
ex.82: GS out ≈ 84 kt, GS home ≈ 115 kt. Time out = 2 h × 115 / 199 ≈ 1.16 h → ≈ 97 NM.
ex.88: QFE 963 is 50 hPa below 1013, about 1400 ft at roughly 28 ft/hPa near the ground, so the 1013 altimeter shows about 5000 + 1400 = 6400 ft.
ex.91: FL75 with QNH 1023 is about 7500 + 300 = 7800 ft amsl; minus the 1500 ft elevation = 6300 ft to climb.
ex.92: 36 min with a 60 kt tailwind adds 36 NM: 157 + 36 = 193 NM.
ex.93: For a given course, drift is greatest with the wind at 90° to it: 040 + 90 = 130°.
